factors.name: Extrinsic
factors.description: A strong orientation for external validation, incentive and recognition from other people. It includes a feeling of gratification from formal and informal rewards, artifacts of status and feeling for progression and progress in ones job. People who are extrinsically motivated typically pursue a task or activity in anticipation of a positive outcome or a avoidance of a negative consequence.

factors.name: Flexibility
factors.description: A positive orientation towards change characterised by an awareness and a willingness to adapt to working in different situations with different people and under different priorities. People high on flexibility are more accommodating and more open to perspectives, ideas and differing scenarios.

factors.name: Ambition
factors.description: The extent to which an individual is defined by a high need to achieve and attain success in one’s work and life outcomes.

factors.name: Values
factors.description: The core beliefs which are at the heart of driving genuine consistency in the individual. It is an awareness and sensitivity to the congruence between stated values and what is demonstrated on the job.

factors.name: Empathy
factors.description: The degree to which the one is aware of and focused on the thoughts, feelings and preferences of others. People high on empathy always take other peoples emotions into consideration while working, and especially when making decisions and assessing the impact of those choices on others.

factors.name: Teamwork
factors.description: A high need for synergy and collaboration, in which one prefers to work collectively with others to perform and be effective. Being part of a team and working with others allows the individual to be at their best. It leads to a sense of activation and need for nurturance from others.

factors.name: Autonomy
factors.description: Is the desire and willingness to be independent and self-sufficient. To complete work tasks and deliver results in a manner and pace set by oneself , without the need for direction and supervision from others.

factors.name: Extra-Role
factors.description: The willingness to exert additional effort in going above and beyond what is normally expected from one’s job. It is the fulfilment gained by exceeding set or stated expectations and the focus on thinking about putting in discretionary effort in pursuing the end rather than only contributing to the means.

factors.name: Intrinsic
factors.description: Is derived from an internal sense of passion, purpose and meaning f or what one does and why one does it, without too much consideration for the end goal or the result. External aspects such as reward and recognition take a backseat as compared to an drive and passion to pursue goals and priorities that are important to oneself versus other people.

factors.name: Energy
factors.description: An approach to life and one’s work with anticipation, enthusiasm and excitement. This excitement will be clearly visible to others at work and of ten have a positive, uplifting impact. It involves a high state of being alert, active and full of life.

factors.name: Zest
factors.description: A sense of enjoyment and engagement with one’s work and current role. It’s the feeling of wanting to work and contribute to one's job on most days, which is affirming and energizing.

factors.name: Growth
factors.description: A strong belief that people have the innate potential and capacity to develop for the better, if they so desire. It is a belief that change is possible, that if people invest the necessary effort, apply their energy and focus, they can improve their abilities and capabilities. This is in contrast to having a ‘rigid’ view of the world assuming that capabilities are relatively fixed, and hard to change, no matter what people do.

factors.name: Curiosity
factors.description: A strong orientation and interest in discovering more about work and the extent to which new learning is actively sought out in one’s role or broader work environment. It is characterised by thriving in situations where there is an opportunity to be inquisitive and investigating further.

factors.name: Analytical
factors.description: The capacity to fully understand the nature of the task, issue or project at work in a logical and in-depth manner. It is driven by an innate need f or being able to understand how and why something works or does not work as a key to individual satisfaction and sense of effectiveness.

factors.name: Confidence
factors.description: A positive self-evaluation of oneself and in one’s abilities to deal with any situation at work and / or in life. It is an appreciative self-image in feeling self-assured, secure and undaunted while dealing with people and challenges at work. A feeling of confidence is directly related to one’s self-esteem.

factors.name: Preparedness
factors.description: An affirmative judgment of how well one’s own skills and experience stack-up to performing in one’s job or role within the organisation, leading to a sense of readiness for work. Believing that one’s skills compare favourably to other’s performing similar roles anywhere in the world.

factors.name: Control
factors.description: A single-minded focus and pursuit of work goals and activities within one’s immediate area of impact. It is driven by a strong desire of wanting to be in command. It typically leads to filtering of attention and effort on aspects that are within one’s direct sphere of influence, with less regard for things that can not be impacted directly. For people with high control, a lack of opportunity to be in-charge of their own priorities can lead to a sense of anxiousness.

factors.name: Mastery
factors.description: A high need to achieve excellence. A focus on continuous improvement, to get better in one’s specific area of work or interest. It is dominated by a feeling of dissatisfaction with complacency and mediocrity from oneself and others.

factors.name: Absorption
factors.description: The capacity to experience being fully engrossed in a task or activity, often losing track of time. Often described as being in ‘flow’. It is a sense of complete concentration, which is transcendental in nature, with minimal attention to one’s surroundings, circumstances or other people for extended time periods.

factors.name: Ethics
factors.description: The standards of conduct and action by which the individual expects to hold oneself and others at work. It is a heightened sense of workplace behaviors and an expectation for others to abide by them.

factors.name: Responsibility
factors.description: The sense of ownership and willingness to be held responsible f or one’s own results and performance as well as for the quality and quantity of others’ work. Often times, this involves taking a more ‘leading’ and visible role in impacting things that matter, versus simply being a ‘supporter’ or ‘bystander’ in the process.

factors.name: Conviction
factors.description: A strong belief in one’s opinions and point of view. It is the willingness and courage to stand up for oneself in the face of opposition and / or lack of support. People with a strong sense of conviction have the fervor and capacity to stick to their own viewpoint even if its unpopular.

factors.name: Ambiguity
factors.description: The level of comfort in dealing with uncertainty. It is the capacity to work through situations where there is limited information, where outcomes are unclear and / or where there is a lack of clear processes and procedures. It involves one’s sense of perspective and judgment to follow through when the circumstances may be very new or different or vague.

factors.name: Creativity
factors.description: The desire and orientation to innovate, generate new ideas and concepts, demonstrate original thinking and implement them at the workplace. To push oneself and others to identity new, different and / or unique ways of working, leading to a sense of boredom with all things routine and process-driven.

factors.name: Sales Relationships
factors.description: Displays an empathetic approach with others. Establishes, develops and maintains networks.

factors.name: Sales Tenacity
factors.description: Demonstrates resilience during difficult times. Displays tenacity when facing challenging obstacles.

factors.name: Customer Service
factors.description: Displays confidence in own abilities to understand the customer and provide exceptional service

factors.name: Customer Centricity
factors.description: Understands and responds to customer needs. Takes ownership for appropriate action

factors.name: Customer Tenacity
factors.description: Demonstrates resilience in the face of challenging situations. Shows determination and persistence to achieve goals

factors.name: Customer Relationships
factors.description: Appreciates problems and issues from the perspective of customers. Goes the extra mile to meet customer needs

factors.name: Customer Happiness
factors.description: Displays a positive and enthusiastic approach to dealing with customers. Displays energy and passion towards work

factors.name: Grit
factors.description: The capacity to persevere with a difficult task, person or situation at work with a strong belief that effort and persistence will get the necessary results. There is an important element of being able to follow through on goals and objectives till the end, and not give up half-way. It’s the resolve and will-power to endure despite the circumstances.

factors.name: Resilience
factors.description: The resilience to bounce back from setbacks and missed opportunities, with a fresh appetite to try again. Previous failures are seen as a means to learn from mistakes and as a way to learn and grow from challenges or difficult circumstances. It is the capacity to cope with stress, high demands and / or adversity, and not be overwhelmed by the situation at hand.

It is a favorable perspective on life and work events and the attitude to always see the brighter side of things.

It typically leads to filtering of attention and effort on aspects that are within one’s direct sphere of influence, with less regard for things that can not be impacted directly. For people with high control, a lack of opportunity to be in-charge of their own priorities can lead to a sense of anxiousness.

factors.name: Responsibility
factors.description: The sense of ownership and willingness to be held responsible f or one’s own results and performance as well as for the quality and quantity of others’ work. Often times, this involves taking a more ‘leading’ and visible role in impacting things that matter, versus simply being a ‘supporter’ or ‘bystander’ in the process.

factors.name: Preparedness
factors.description: An affirmative judgment of how well one’s own skills and experience stack-up to performing in one’s job or role within the organisation, leading to a sense of readiness for work. Believing that one’s skills compare favourably to other’s performing similar roles anywhere in the world.

factors.name: Conviction
factors.description: A strong belief in one’s opinions and point of view. It is the willingness and courage to stand up for oneself in the face of opposition and / or lack of support. People with a strong sense of conviction have the fervor and capacity to stick to their own viewpoint even if its unpopular.

factors.name: Ambiguity
factors.description: The level of comfort in dealing with uncertainty. It is the capacity to work through situations where there is limited information, where outcomes are unclear and / or where there is a lack of clear processes and procedures. It involves one’s sense of perspective and judgment to follow through when the circumstances may be very new or different or vague.

factors.name: Empathy
factors.description: The degree to which the one is aware of and focused on the thoughts, feelings and preferences of others. People high on empathy always take other peoples emotions into consideration while working, and especially when making decisions and assessing the impact of those choices on others.

It typically leads to filtering of attention and effort on aspects that are within one’s direct sphere of influence, with less regard for things that can not be impacted directly. For people with high control, a lack of opportunity to be in-charge of their own priorities can lead to a sense of anxiousness.

factors.name: Teamwork
factors.description: A high need for synergy and collaboration, in which one prefers to work collectively with others to perform and be effective. Being part of a team and working with others allows the individual to be at their best. It leads to a sense of activation and need for nurturance from others.

factors.name: Autonomy
factors.description: Is the desire and willingness to be independent and self-sufficient. To complete work tasks and deliver results in a manner and pace set by oneself , without the need for direction and supervision from others.

factors.name: Values
factors.description: The core beliefs which are at the heart of driving genuine consistency in the individual. It is an awareness and sensitivity to the congruence between stated values and what is demonstrated on the job.

factors.name: Ethics
factors.description: The standards of conduct and action by which the individual expects to hold oneself and others at work. It is a heightened sense of workplace behaviors and an expectation for others to abide by them.

factors.name: Ambition
factors.description: The extent to which an individual is defined by a high need to achieve and attain success in one’s work and life outcomes.

factors.name: Mastery
factors.description: A high need to achieve excellence. A focus on continuous improvement, to get better in one’s specific area of work or interest. It is dominated by a feeling of dissatisfaction with complacency and mediocrity from oneself and others.

factors.name: Absorption
factors.description: The capacity to experience being fully engrossed in a task or activity, often losing track of time. Often described as being in ‘flow’. It is a sense of complete concentration, which is transcendental in nature, with minimal attention to one’s surroundings, circumstances or other people for extended time periods.

factors.name: Extrinsic
factors.description: A strong orientation for external validation, incentive and recognition from other people. It includes a feeling of gratification from formal and informal rewards, artifacts of status and feeling for progression and progress in ones job. People who are extrinsically motivated typically pursue a task or activity in anticipation of a positive outcome or a avoidance of a negative consequence.

factors.name: Extra-Role
factors.description: The willingness to exert additional effort in going above and beyond what is normally expected from one’s job. It is the fulfilment gained by exceeding set or stated expectations and the focus on thinking about putting in discretionary effort in pursuing the end rather than only contributing to the means.

factors.name: Intrinsic
factors.description: Is derived from an internal sense of passion, purpose and meaning f or what one does and why one does it, without too much consideration for the end goal or the result. External aspects such as reward and recognition take a backseat as compared to an drive and passion to pursue goals and priorities that are important to oneself versus other people.

factors.name: Confidence
factors.description: A positive self-evaluation of oneself and in one’s abilities to deal with any situation at work and / or in life. It is an appreciative self-image in feeling self-assured, secure and undaunted while dealing with people and challenges at work. A feeling of confidence is directly related to one’s self-esteem.

factors.name: Grit
factors.description: The capacity to persevere with a difficult task, person or situation at work with a strong belief that effort and persistence will get the necessary results. There is an important element of being able to follow through on goals and objectives till the end, and not give up half-way. It’s the resolve and will-power to endure despite the circumstances.

factors.name: Resilience
factors.description: The resilience to bounce back from setbacks and missed opportunities, with a fresh appetite to try again. Previous failures are seen as a means to learn from mistakes and as a way to learn and grow from challenges or difficult circumstances. It is the capacity to cope with stress, high demands and / or adversity, and not be overwhelmed by the situation at hand.

factors.name: Curiosity
factors.description: A strong orientation and interest in discovering more about work and the extent to which new learning is actively sought out in one’s role or broader work environment. It is characterised by thriving in situations where there is an opportunity to be inquisitive and investigating further.

factors.name: Analytical
factors.description: The capacity to fully understand the nature of the task, issue or project at work in a logical and in-depth manner. It is driven by an innate need f or being able to understand how and why something works or does not work as a key to individual satisfaction and sense of effectiveness.

factors.name: Creativity
factors.description: The desire and orientation to innovate, generate new ideas and concepts, demonstrate original thinking and implement them at the workplace. To push oneself and others to identity new, different and / or unique ways of working, leading to a sense of boredom with all things routine and process-driven.

It is the capacity to cope with stress, high demands and / or adversity, and not be overwhelmed by the situation at hand.

factors.name: Flexibility
factors.description: A positive orientation towards change characterised by an awareness and a willingness to adapt to working in different situations with different people and under different priorities. People high on flexibility are more accommodating and more open to perspectives, ideas and differing scenarios.

factors.name: Growth
factors.description: A strong belief that people have the innate potential and capacity to develop for the better, if they so desire. It is a belief that change is possible, that if people invest the necessary effort, apply their energy and focus, they can improve their abilities and capabilities. This is in contrast to having a ‘rigid’ view of the world assuming that capabilities are relatively fixed, and hard to change, no matter what people do.

factors.name: Energy
factors.description: An approach to life and one’s work with anticipation, enthusiasm and excitement. This excitement will be clearly visible to others at work and of ten have a positive, uplifting impact. It involves a high state of being alert, active and full of life.

factors.name: Zest
factors.description: A sense of enjoyment and engagement with one’s work and current role. It’s the feeling of wanting to work and contribute to one's job on most days, which is affirming and energizing.

factors.name: Optimism
factors.description: The degree of optimism that one has towards work, which may extend to other facets of lif e as well. People with a high sense of positivity have the worldview that the glass is always half full. It is a favorable perspective on life and work events and the attitude to always see the brighter side of things.

props.questionText:
Welcome to your Thriving Index questionnaire - hosted by the Talent Enterprise.

This questionnaire will ask you about your attitudes, preferences and orientation towards your job or education. It has approximately 95 questions, with some additional demographic questions towards the end and will take an estimated 15-20 minutes to complete.

Some things to remember:

a) Do answer the survey as honestly as you can. Please remember that there are no right or wrong answers

b) While completing the questions, respond instinctively with the first response that comes to your mind

c) Try and complete the questionnaire in one-go, preferably without any interruptions Instructions: Please read and consider each question individually, and answer it as honestly as possible by clicking the button next to the choice you want. When you have answered every question on the page, click the "Next" button on the lower right of the screen to move on to the next page.

NOTE: You must answer every question on each page before you can move on. If you have any questions or require any clarifications regarding this questionnaire, please write to us at surveys@thetalententerprise.com
